## Step 1: Develop initial scraper and crawler

```{python}
import re
from urllib.parse import urljoin

import requests
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# target page
URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
BASE = "https://oig.hhs.gov"

# headers with user-agent
headers = {
    "User-Agent": "DAP30538CourseBot/1.0 (yanjiec@uchicago.edu)"
}

# get the page
resp = requests.get(URL, headers=headers, timeout=30)
resp.raise_for_status()

# parse the page using BeautifulSoup
soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "lxml")

# types in the page "Type" filter
KNOWN_TYPES = {
    "Child Support",
    "CIA Reportable Events",
    "CMP and Affirmative Exclusions",
    "COVID-19",
    "Criminal and Civil Actions",
    "EMTALA/Patient Dumping",
    "Fraud Self-Disclosures",
    "Grant and Contractor Fraud Self-Disclosures",
    "State Enforcement Agencies",
    "Stipulated Penalties and Material Breaches",
}

# I asked ChatGPT how to extract the date from the page, and it suggested using a regex by first finding the months in the page text and then compile the regex for the date using the syntax of the regex module in Python
# regex for date
MONTHS = r"(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)"
DATE_RE = re.compile(rf"{MONTHS}\s+\d{{1,2}},\s+\d{{4}}")

# initialize empty list to store the data
rows = []

# I asked ChatGPT how to write <a href> in the regex, and it suggested using a[href]
# action title in <h2>, <h2> contains <a href>
# find all <h2> that contains <a href>
h2_links = soup.select("h2 a[href]")
for a in h2_links:
    title = a.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    # connect the base URL with the link
    link = urljoin(BASE, a.get("href"))

    # I asked ChatGPT how to find the parent container, and it suggested using the find_parent method
    # find the parent container
    container = a.find_parent(["li", "div"])
    if container is None:
        continue

    # I asked ChatGPT how to join the text in the container, and it suggested using the strip_strings method
    # join the text in the container
    blob = " ".join(container.stripped_strings)
    # print(blob)

    # find the date: Month Day, Year in the container text
    m = DATE_RE.search(blob)
    # print(m)
    # I asked ChatGPT how to extract the date from a regex search, and it suggested using the group method
    # extract the date from the container text
    date = m.group(0) if m else None

    # category: find the types in the container text
    cats = []
    for t in KNOWN_TYPES:
        if t in blob:
            cats.append(t)
    
    # remove duplicates and sort by the order of appearance in the blob
    if cats:
        cats = sorted(set(cats), key=lambda x: blob.find(x))
        category = "; ".join(cats)
    else:
        category = None

    # only collect the items that have date and at least one category
    if date and category:
        rows.append(
            {
                "title": title,
                "date": date,
                "category": category,
                "link": link,
            }
        )

    # only collect 20 items on the first page
    if len(rows) >= 20:
        break

# convert to dataframe
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

# print dataframe heads
print(df.head())
```

## Step 2: Making the scraper dynamic

### 1. Turning the scraper into a function 

* a. Pseudo-Code
```{text}
FUNCTION scrape_enforcement_actions(month, year, run_scraper):
BEGIN
    IF year < 2013 THEN
        PRINT "Please restrict to year >= 2013..."
        RETURN None
    END IF

    SET outfile TO "enforcement_actions_year_month.csv"

    IF run_scraper IS FALSE THEN
        IF outfile EXISTS THEN
            READ outfile AS dataframe
            RETURN dataframe
        ELSE
            PRINT "run_scraper=False and no cached csv found..."
            RETURN empty dataframe
        END IF
    END IF

    SET start_date TO first day of (year, month)
    SET base_url TO "https://oig.hhs.gov"
    SET current_url TO "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
    SET results TO empty list

    WHILE current_url IS NOT None DO:
        REQUEST current_url (with headers)
        PARSE html WITH BeautifulSoup

        EXTRACT all enforcement action items on this page
        FOR EACH item DO:
            PARSE title, link, date, category FROM item
            CONVERT date string TO date object

            IF item_date >= start_date THEN
                APPEND {title, date, category, link} TO results
            END IF
        END FOR

        IF oldest date on this page < start_date THEN
            BREAK
        END IF

        FIND next page link
        IF next link EXISTS THEN
            SET current_url TO absolute next link
            SLEEP 1 second
        ELSE
            SET current_url TO None
        END IF
    END WHILE

    CONVERT results TO dataframe
    SAVE dataframe TO outfile AS csv
    RETURN dataframe
END
END FUNCTION
```

* b. Create Dynamic Scraper

```{python}
import re
import time
from datetime import datetime, date
from urllib.parse import urljoin

import requests
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

# same setup as Step 1
URL = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
BASE = "https://oig.hhs.gov"

headers = {
    "User-Agent": "DAP30538CourseBot/1.0 (yanjiec@uchicago.edu)"
}

KNOWN_TYPES = {
    "Child Support",
    "CIA Reportable Events",
    "CMP and Affirmative Exclusions",
    "COVID-19",
    "Criminal and Civil Actions",
    "EMTALA/Patient Dumping",
    "Fraud Self-Disclosures",
    "Grant and Contractor Fraud Self-Disclosures",
    "State Enforcement Agencies",
    "Stipulated Penalties and Material Breaches",
}

MONTHS = r"(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)"
DATE_RE = re.compile(rf"{MONTHS}\s+\d{{1,2}},\s+\d{{4}}")

# convert 'Month Day, Year' to datetime.date
def _parse_date_str(date_str: str) -> date | None:
    if not date_str:
        return None
    return datetime.strptime(date_str, "%B %d, %Y").date()

# find the next page url
def _find_next_page_url(soup: BeautifulSoup, current_url: str) -> str | None:
    a = soup.select_one("ul.pagination li.next-page a.pagination-next[href]")
    if a and a.get("href"):
        return urljoin(current_url, a["href"])

    a = soup.select_one("ul.pagination li.next-page a[href]")
    if a and a.get("href"):
        return urljoin(current_url, a["href"])

    return None

# scrape the enforcement actions
def scrape_enforcement_actions(month: int, year: int, run_scraper: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    if year < 2013:
        print("Please restrict to year >= 2013, since only enforcement actions after 2013 are listed.")
        return None

    start_date = date(year, month, 1)
    outfile = f"enforcement_actions_{year}_{month:02d}.csv"

    if not run_scraper:
        try:
            df_cached = pd.read_csv(outfile)
            # parse date column back to datetime.date
            df_cached["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df_cached["date"], errors="coerce")
            print(f"run_scraper=False, so loaded cached csv: {outfile}")
            return df_cached
        except FileNotFoundError:
            print(f"run_scraper=False and no cached csv found: {outfile}")
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=["title", "date", "category", "link"])

    # initialize empty list to store the data
    results = []
    current_url = URL

    while current_url is not None:
        resp = requests.get(current_url, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "lxml")

        # use the same selection rule as Step 1
        h2_links = soup.select("h2 a[href]")

        # track the oldest date on this page
        page_dates = []

        for a in h2_links:
            title = a.get_text(" ", strip=True)
            link = urljoin(BASE, a.get("href"))

            container = a.find_parent(["li", "div"])
            if container is None:
                continue

            blob = " ".join(container.stripped_strings)

            # date by regex
            m = DATE_RE.search(blob)
            date_str = m.group(0) if m else None
            d = _parse_date_str(date_str)

            # category by matching KNOWN_TYPES
            cats = []
            for t in KNOWN_TYPES:
                if t in blob:
                    cats.append(t)

            if cats:
                cats = sorted(set(cats), key=lambda x: blob.find(x))
                category = "; ".join(cats)
            else:
                category = None

            # only keep valid items
            if d and category:
                page_dates.append(d)

                # keep only since start_date
                if d >= start_date:
                    results.append(
                        {
                            "title": title,
                            "date": d.isoformat(),   # save as ISO string
                            "category": category,
                            "link": link,
                        }
                    )

        # if the oldest date on this page is already older than start_date, stop
        if page_dates and min(page_dates) < start_date:
            break

        # go next page
        next_url = _find_next_page_url(soup, current_url)
        if next_url:
            time.sleep(1)
            current_url = next_url
        else:
            current_url = None

    # convert to dataframe and drop duplicates
    df = pd.DataFrame(results).drop_duplicates()
    df.to_csv(outfile, index=False)
    print(f"Saved: {outfile} (rows={len(df)})")
    return df

# run the scraper since Jan 2024
df_2024 = scrape_enforcement_actions(month=1, year=2024, run_scraper=False)

# print the number of enforcement actions
print("Total enforcement actions since Jan 2024:", len(df_2024))

# print the earliest date and details
df_2024["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df_2024["date"], errors="coerce")
earliest_date = df_2024["date"].min()
print("Earliest date scraped:", earliest_date.date())

earliest_rows = (
    df_2024[df_2024["date"] == earliest_date]
    .sort_values(["title"])
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

print("\nEarliest enforcement action(s) details:")
print(earliest_rows[["title", "date", "category", "link"]])
```

## Step 3: Plot data based on scraped data

### 1. Plot the number of enforcement actions over time

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()

# read the cached csv
df = pd.read_csv("enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv")

# ISO dates
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"], errors="coerce")

# aggregate to month-year
monthly = (
    df.assign(year_month=lambda x: x["date"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp())
      .groupby("year_month", as_index=False)
      .size()
      .rename(columns={"size": "n_actions"})
      .sort_values("year_month")
)

# print the first few rows
print(monthly.head())

# make a line chart
chart = alt.Chart(monthly).mark_line().encode(
          x=alt.X(
              "year_month:T", title="Month-Year",
              axis=alt.Axis(
                  format="%Y-%m",
                  tickCount="month",
                  tickMinStep=3  # every 3 months
              )
          ),
          y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of enforcement actions"),
          tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("year_month:T", title="Month", format="%Y-%m"),
                   alt.Tooltip("n_actions:Q", title="Actions")]
      ).properties(
        title="HHS OIG Enforcement Actions per Month + Year (since Jan 2022)",
        width=700,
        height=400
      )

chart.show()
chart.save("chart1.png", engine="vl-convert")
```

### 2. Plot the number of enforcement actions categorized:

* based on "Criminal and Civil Actions" vs. "State Enforcement Agencies"

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()

# read the cached csv
df = pd.read_csv("enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv")

# ISO dates
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"], errors="coerce")
df = df.dropna(subset=["date"])

# month-year to timestamp
df["year_month"] = df["date"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp()

# the two categories to keep
cats_keep = ["Criminal and Civil Actions", "State Enforcement Agencies"]

# aggregate to month-year
monthly_cat = (
    df[df["category"].isin(cats_keep)]
      .groupby(["year_month", "category"], as_index=False)
      .size()
      .rename(columns={"size": "n_actions"})
      .sort_values(["year_month", "category"])
)

# make a line chart
chart_a = alt.Chart(monthly_cat).mark_line().encode(
          x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month-Year",
              axis=alt.Axis(format="%Y-%m", tickCount="month", tickMinStep=3)
          ),
          y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of enforcement actions"),
          color=alt.Color("category:N", title="Category"),
          tooltip=[
              alt.Tooltip("year_month:T", title="Month", format="%Y-%m"),
              alt.Tooltip("category:N", title="Category"),
              alt.Tooltip("n_actions:Q", title="Actions"),
          ],
      ).properties(
          title="Enforcement Actions per Month: Criminal & Civil vs State Enforcement Agencies (since Jan 2022)",
          width=800,
          height=400
      )

chart_a.show()
chart_a.save("chart2.png", engine="vl-convert")
```

* based on five topics

```{python}
import re

# classify the topics
# I asked ChatGPT to give me several words that are related to each topic, and then I used the regex to classify the topics.
def classify_topic(title: str) -> str:
    t = str(title).lower()

    # Bribery/Corruption
    if re.search(r"\b(bribe|bribery|kickback|corrupt|corruption|extortion|quid pro quo)\b", t):
        return "Bribery/Corruption"

    # Drug Enforcement
    if re.search(r"\b(drug|opioid|fentanyl|oxycodone|hydrocodone|pill mill|controlled substance|dea)\b", t):
        return "Drug Enforcement"

    # Financial Fraud
    if re.search(r"\b(bank|bankrupt|wire fraud|money laundering|launder|embezzle|investment|securities|loan|tax|irs|identity theft|credit|mortgage|financial)\b", t):
        return "Financial Fraud"

    # Health Care Fraud
    if re.search(r"\b(medicare|medicaid|health care|healthcare|claims?|billing|billings|provider|hospital|clinic|pharmacy|home health|hospice|dme|durable medical|lab|laboratory)\b", t):
        return "Health Care Fraud"

    # Other
    return "Other"

# filter the data to only include "Criminal and Civil Actions"
df_cc = df[df["category"] == "Criminal and Civil Actions"].copy()
# classify the topics
df_cc["topic"] = df_cc["title"].apply(classify_topic)

# aggregate to month-year
monthly_topic = (
    df_cc.groupby(["year_month", "topic"], as_index=False)
         .size()
         .rename(columns={"size": "n_actions"})
         .sort_values(["year_month", "topic"])
)

# the order of the topics in the legend
topic_order = ["Health Care Fraud", "Financial Fraud", "Drug Enforcement", "Bribery/Corruption", "Other"]

# make a line chart
chart_b = alt.Chart(monthly_topic).mark_line().encode(
          x=alt.X("year_month:T", title="Month-Year",
              axis=alt.Axis(format="%Y-%m", tickCount="month", tickMinStep=3)
          ),
          y=alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of enforcement actions"),
          color=alt.Color("topic:N", sort=topic_order, title="Topic"),
          tooltip=[
              alt.Tooltip("year_month:T", title="Month", format="%Y-%m"),
              alt.Tooltip("topic:N", title="Topic"),
              alt.Tooltip("n_actions:Q", title="Actions"),
          ],
      ).properties(
          title="Criminal and Civil Actions per Month + Year, by Topic (since Jan 2022)",
          width=800,
          height=400
      )

chart_b.show()
chart_b.save("chart3.png", engine="vl-convert")
```
